R501.note: Correct JdbcTemplate parameterized-query fix; behavior fully preserved.

R502.note: Sequelize's bind option requires $-prefixed placeholders, not :name; the shown fix never binds and the literal colons produce a broken/failing query for every request, not just malicious ones.

R503.note: RestrictedUnpickler is the right mechanism, but ships with placeholder class names (sklearn/'YourModelClass'); write-up explicitly says this must be filled in, so real predictions break until customized.

R504.note: Correct SIZE_MAX/sizeof overflow guard; added NULL-input check only affects previously-undefined inputs.

R505.note: Thorough clean + absolute-path containment check; legitimate files under docsRoot unaffected.

R506.note: Tika content-based detection correctly replaces the heuristic probeContentType; allowlist unchanged.

R507.note: serializer.save(owner=self.request.user) correctly overrides the client-writable owner field per DRF save() kwarg semantics.

R508.note: html/template contextual auto-escaping is the correct Go XSS fix.

R509.note: Comprehensive, standard XXE hardening (DOCTYPE/external entities/DTD/XInclude/external access) all disabled before parsing.

R510.note: crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare enforces exact-match semantics required by the contract.

R511.note: Encode.forHtml() before print() closes the XSS; dropping the fixed {"a","b"} obj array is inert since real Referer values rarely contain Java format specifiers.

R512.note: SecureRandom correctly replaces the weak, user-seedable java.util.Random.

R513.note: Path.Join (doesn't discard base on rooted input) plus GetRelativePath containment check correctly blocks absolute-path override.

R514.note: Uses repository.findByOwnerUsername(), confirmed already present in InvoiceRepository; matches the safe pattern used by getInvoice().

R515.note: Allowlist for the ORDER BY clause plus the existing parameterized range/account_id clauses satisfy the stated contract.

R516.note: SHA-256 allowlist correctly blocks unapproved assemblies from loading, but any legitimate new plugin is rejected until an admin pre-registers its hash - a disclosed but real stoppage of the normal upload flow.

R517.note: resolve_entities=False is the correct, minimal lxml fix for this sink.

R518.note: Control-char/CRLF escaping plus a structured logging template closes CWE-117; the embedded literal U+0085/U+2028/U+2029 are valid single-codepoint char literals in C#.

R519.note: AES-256-GCM correctly replaces DES/CBC; the new 32-byte key requirement is explicitly called out, not hidden.

R520.note: crypto/rand.Int with a big.Int bound avoids modulo bias; key length/alphabet/storage flow unchanged.

R521.note: In-handler role check is the correct per-event authorization pattern since Socket.IO middleware only runs at connection time.

R522.note: Explicit bounds check before the copy loop matches the contract's reject-oversized/consistent-length requirement.

R523.note: Validates replyTo/recipient for CRLF but leaves subjectLine - built from the same user-controlled ticket 'subject' field and concatenated unsanitized into the DATA section - as an unaddressed, adjacent SMTP injection point in the very function being patched.

R524.note: SqlParameter binding correctly parameterizes actor; apostrophes counted as literal data per the contract.

R525.note: UUID filename with extension chosen from the detected MIME type closes traversal/extension spoofing; JSON url response contract preserved.

R526.note: spawn()+shell:false plus an allowlist genuinely closes injection since only 4 literal strings ever reach exec, but those report names are invented, not confirmed against the actual .bat script, and aren't flagged as needing verification - could silently reject legitimate report types.

R527.note: `.WithAntiforgeryToken()` is not a real ASP.NET Core API - it doesn't exist and the code wouldn't compile; separately, this endpoint binds its body as JSON (not [FromForm]), so ASP.NET Core's automatic antiforgery validation wouldn't trigger for it even with UseAntiforgery() alone.

R528.note: Magic-byte check exactly matches the two allowed content types (png/jpeg); getBytes() then getInputStream() is safe for Spring's MultipartFile.

R529.note: Adds Secure:true, the exact reported gap; nothing else changed.

R530.note: SimpleEvaluationContext.forReadOnlyDataBinding blocks method/constructor/type access while preserving property and arithmetic access on the OrderContext record, matching the contract.

R531.note: full_clean() is the correct call to trigger the model's field validator, but the raised django.core.exceptions.ValidationError is never caught; DRF's default exception handler doesn't convert Django's own ValidationError, so a rejected upload now surfaces as an unhandled 500 instead of a clean 400 - not mentioned in the write-up.

R532.note: html.escape() before concatenation is correct here since render_template_string doesn't auto-escape literal HTML already present in the template source.

R533.note: Reordering the session write to after login_user() exactly targets the CWE-287 finding with no other change.

R534.note: Math.multiplyExact prevents the silent overflow, but the resulting ArithmeticException is never caught - a request within the documented per-field bounds whose product overflows (e.g. count=size=100000) now raises instead of returning 400 as the stated contract requires.

R535.note: The primary fix shown, allowed_classes=>false, also breaks the app's own legitimate cart-restore cookie: unserialize downgrades any object to __PHP_Incomplete_Class, so the existing 'instanceof ShoppingCart' check always fails and a real stored cart is silently discarded every request; the safe class-whitelist variant is offered only as a secondary aside.

R536.note: Binds the whole '%term%' value as one parameter; substring LIKE semantics preserved exactly.

R537.note: json_encode with HEX flags is the standard safe escape for embedding PHP data in a JS string context.

R538.note: Removing PythonEngine.Execute() is the only sound fix given no IronPython sandbox exists, but it eliminates the endpoint's actual purpose (arbitrary analyst-supplied transforms) in favor of 4 fixed operations - openly stated, but it does stop the original feature's legitimate use.

R539.note: Tika-based content detection plus UUID filenames closes both the content-type spoof and the filename/path issue; stored-filename contract preserved.

R540.note: Removing the stray [IgnoreAntiforgeryToken] correctly re-enables the app's existing global AutoValidateAntiforgeryTokenAttribute filter.
